pages.hook: In English, the days of the week always start with a capital letter, and many have names from old gods. Learn the week and how to make plans.

mythfact.s: Days of the week start with a capital letter in English.
mythfact.why: We write Monday, Friday, Sunday, not monday.

mythfact.s: Sunday is named after the Sun.
mythfact.why: Sunday = “Sun’s day”. Monday = “Moon’s day”.

mythfact.s: The word Thursday comes from the Roman god Jupiter.
mythfact.why: Thursday comes from Thor, the Norse god of thunder. (Latin had Jupiter’s day, and Thor is the Norse match for Jupiter.)

mythfact.s: In many US calendars, the week starts on Sunday.
mythfact.why: Many printed calendars in the USA begin with Sunday, not Monday.

mythfact.s: San Francisco’s Golden Gate Bridge opened in 1937.
mythfact.why: It opened in May 1937.

pages.title: Reading quest — My week in San Francisco · part 1
text: I live in San Francisco, a city with steep hills and a red bridge called the Golden Gate. It opened in 1937. Today my friend Nina asks me, “**What day is it today?**” “**It’s Monday**,” I say.

“**Oh no!** **I have class on Mondays**,” says Nina. “**When do you have class?**” I ask. “**On Monday and Wednesday**,” she says. I have yoga on **Friday**. “Come with me!” I tell her. “**Great! What time?**” she asks. “**At six in the evening**,” I say. “**See you on Friday!**”

I like Fridays, but many people do not like Mondays. In 1979, an Irish band, The Boomtown Rats, made a song called “I Don’t Like Mondays”. It was a big hit in the United Kingdom. Today the title is a common phrase for people who find the start of the week hard.

text: Here is my week. On Monday I study. On Tuesday I work. On Wednesday I walk by the sea. On Thursday I cook. On Friday I do yoga. On the **weekend**, I rest, see friends and sometimes ride a cable car.
A good plan makes the week easier. When I **check the calendar**, I feel calm. Every week has hard days, but it also has fun days.

pages.title: Reading quest · Talk about it
text: I live in San Francisco, a city with steep hills and a red bridge called the Golden Gate. It opened in 1937. Today my friend Nina asks me, “**What day is it today?**” “**It’s Monday**,” I say.

“**Oh no!** **I have class on Mondays**,” says Nina. “**When do you have class?**” I ask. “**On Monday and Wednesday**,” she says. I have yoga on **Friday**. “Come with me!” I tell her. “**Great! What time?**” she asks. “**At six in the evening**,” I say. “**See you on Friday!**”

I like Fridays, but many people do not like Mondays. In 1979, an Irish band, The Boomtown Rats, made a song called “I Don’t Like Mondays”. It was a big hit in the United Kingdom. Today the title is a common phrase for people who find the start of the week hard.
Here is my week. On Monday I study. On Tuesday I work. On Wednesday I walk by the sea. On Thursday I cook. On Friday I do yoga. On the **weekend**, I rest, see friends and sometimes ride a cable car.
A good plan makes the week easier. When I **check the calendar**, I feel calm. Every week has hard days, but it also has fun days.
